title: Existence of the normalized scalar-extension twist comparison
statement: Let $R,S,A,B$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $S$, an $R$-algebra structure on $A$, and an $S$-algebra structure on $B$. Let $A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}A_n$ and $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}B_n$ be graded rings with $A_n$ an $R$-submodule and $B_n$ an $S$-submodule. Fix ring maps $\rho_A:R\to A_0$ and $\rho_B:S\to B_0$ whose composites into $A$ and $B$ are the specified algebra maps. Let $\beta:S\otimes_R A\simeq B$ be an $S$-algebra isomorphism and $\psi:A\to B$ a graded ring map such that $\beta(1\otimes a)=\psi(a)$ and $B_n=\operatorname{span}_S\psi(A_n)$ for every $n$. Write $P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$, $Q=\operatorname{Proj}(B)$ and use their standard opens and chart inclusions [lem-nagata-affine-proj-scalar-extension], their twisting module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Suppose $r:Q\to P$ satisfies $r^{-1}D_+(f)=D_+(\psi(f))$ for every positive-degree homogeneous $f$, and on this chart is the spectrum map of $A_{(f)}\to B_{(\psi(f))}$ induced by $\psi$. There exists a family of isomorphisms $\theta_j:r^*\mathcal O_P(j)\simeq\mathcal O_Q(j)$, for all $j\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying [def-sfb-proj-scalar-extension-twist-normalization]: for $a\in A_i$, $b\in A_k$, $i=k+j$, $U\subseteq D_+(b)$, and a section $s$ of $\mathcal O_P(j)$ on $U$ with $bs=a$ pointwise, the transported section satisfies $\psi(b)c\theta_j(1\otimes s)=c\psi(a)$ pointwise on $r^{-1}U$ for every coefficient section $c$.

proof.text: Put $V_f=D_+(f)$ and $U_f=D_+(\psi(f))$. The scalar-extension Proj lemma gives $r^{-1}V_f=U_f$, their affine chart ring map, and the covering $Q=\bigcup_fU_f$. The twists are quasi-coherent: apply the graded-module sheaf existence theorem (c) to $A(j)$ and $B(j)$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence. Consequently the affine pullback-sections theorem identifies $\Gamma(U_f,r^*\mathcal O_P(j))$ with $(A_f)_j\otimes_{(A_f)_0}(B_{\psi(f)})_0$, by $(a/f^m)\otimes c\mapsto c\,r^*(a/f^m)$. Its hypotheses hold because both $V_f$ and $U_f$ are affine, $U_f\subseteq r^{-1}V_f$, and $\mathcal O_P(j)$ is quasi-coherent. This applies to every integer $j$, with no assertion that the twist is invertible.

proof.text:
Write $H=(A_f)_0$ and $L_j=(A_f)_j$. The degree-zero localization comparison, followed by $\beta$ on fractions, identifies $(B_{\psi(f)})_0$ with $S\otimes_RH$. There is an explicit isomorphism $L_j\otimes_H(S\otimes_RH)\cong S\otimes_RL_j$: send $u\otimes(s\otimes h)$ to $s\otimes hu$, with inverse $s\otimes u\mapsto u\otimes(s\otimes1)$. These formulas respect the $R$- and $H$-balancing relations and their composites are identities on pure tensors. Apply the homogeneous-module localization comparison to $M=A$ and degree $j$, and then the map on localized modules induced by the graded isomorphism $\beta$. The resulting isomorphism
$$F_{f,j}:L_j\otimes_H(B_{\psi(f)})_0\xrightarrow{\sim}(B_{\psi(f)})_j$$
is exactly $(a/f^m)\otimes c\mapsto c\psi(a)/\psi(f)^m$: first check $c=\beta_f(s\otimes h)$, then use additivity. The extension from pure tensors uses only the balanced tensor relations.

proof.text: On the affine scheme $U_f$, both sheaves in question are quasi-coherent by step 1. The affine tilde--global-sections adjunction, with its isomorphic counit for quasi-coherent modules, therefore turns $F_{f,j}$ into a unique sheaf isomorphism $\theta_{f,j}$. Its inverse is obtained from $F_{f,j}^{-1}$ by the same functor. This supplies the sheaf maps as well as their inverses, rather than just an abstract bijection of section modules.

proof.text: The local maps agree on overlaps. On $U_{fg}=U_f\cap U_g$, a section $a/f^m$ restricts to $ag^m/(fg)^m$; applying either local formula gives $\psi(a)\psi(g)^m/\psi(fg)^m$. For the map from the $g$-chart the identical argument uses $bf^n/(fg)^n$. These checks determine the maps on the entire overlap: by the affine pullback-sections theorem the pullbacks of sections on $V_f$, together with coefficients on $U_{fg}$, generate the source there. Equality on global sections determines maps between these quasi-coherent sheaves on the affine overlap by the affine adjunction. More generally, for $D_+(g)\subseteq D_+(f)$ choose $g^e=hf$ as in the graded-module sheaf theorem (a). Restriction sends $a/f^m$ to $h^ma/g^{em}$, and both orders of restriction and comparison send it to $\psi(h)^m\psi(a)/\psi(g)^{em}$; coefficients restrict by the ring map. Thus all specified standard-open restrictions commute. Glue the $\theta_{f,j}$ by the module-sheaf gluing theorem (1). Their inverses agree as well, since they are inverses to equal maps on overlaps, so gluing them gives the inverse of the resulting canonical $\theta_j^\psi$. The local formula implies the denominator-multiplied normalized equation on any locally represented section, and hence IsScalarExtensionTwistComparison. No uniqueness or multiplicativity conclusion is asserted here.

theorem scalarExtension_twist_exists
    {R S A B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing A] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R S] [Algebra R A] [Algebra S B]
    (𝒜 : ℕ → Submodule R A) (ℬ : ℕ → Submodule S B)
    [GradedRing 𝒜] [GradedRing ℬ]
    (ρA : R →+* 𝒜 0) (ρB : S →+* ℬ 0)
    (hρA : ∀ a : R, (ρA a : A) = algebraMap R A a)
    (hρB : ∀ b : S, (ρB b : B) = algebraMap S B b)
    (β : TensorProduct R S A ≃ₐ[S] B) (ψ : 𝒜 →+*ᵍ ℬ)
    (hβψ : ∀ a : A, β (TensorProduct.tmul R (1 : S) a) = ψ a)
    (hgraded : ∀ n : ℕ, ℬ n = Submodule.span S (ψ '' (𝒜 n : Set A)))
    (r : Proj ℬ ⟶ Proj 𝒜)
    (hpre : ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : A), f ∈ 𝒜 n → 0 < n →
      r ⁻¹ᵁ basicOpen 𝒜 f = basicOpen ℬ (ψ f))
    (hchart : ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : A) (hf : f ∈ 𝒜 n) (hn : 0 < n),
      awayι ℬ (ψ f) (ψ.map_mem hf) hn ≫ r =
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (HomogeneousLocalization.Away.map ψ f)) ≫
          awayι 𝒜 f hf hn):
    ∃ θ : ∀ j : ℤ, (tensorPullback r).obj (twist 𝒜 j) ≅ twist ℬ j,
      IsScalarExtensionTwistComparison ψ r θ
